steps.title: Welkom bij Procest
steps.body: Laten we Procest klaarzetten. Initialiseer eerst het register; laad daarna optioneel de Bezwaar & Beroep voorbeelddata.

steps.title: Welcome to Procest
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through case handling — we'll register a case together so you can see how the pieces fit. You'll add the record yourself.
Cases are the heart of your work. Open Cases from the menu to see everything in progress.
Register your first case — give it a title and pick a case type, then save. You can add tasks, decisions and documents later.
steps.task: Click New and save a case

steps.body: Your work lives here. Open My Work to see the tasks and cases assigned to you.
steps.task: Click My Work in the menu

steps.title: You're all set
steps.body: Nicely done — your first case is on the board. Head back to the Dashboard to track progress, and reopen this tour anytime from the … menu.

config.description: Cases, deadlines and your workload at a glance

config._note: CASE archetype (unified zaak) — the flagship record and the ONLY procest entity that declares comms linkedTypes (mail, calendar, forms, photos, maps, shares), so this is the one detail page that earns Email/Appointments/Forms/Photos/Location leaf tabs. Overview groups data+metadata; the working surface is bespoke tabs — Tasks, Decisions, Besluitvorming (decidesk leaf), Dossier, Advies, Sub-cases and Related-cases (object-list panels filtered by this case id) — plus a per-case locations related-index (location.case=:id) and audit-trail. Rarely-touched leaves (Forms, Photos, Location) sit at the end of the tab order.

sidebarTabs.label: Besluitvorming
sidebarTabs._note: decidesk-owned decision-making leaf (decidesk-decisions): proposals, advice and decisions linked to this case. Replaces the standalone Besluitvorming nav (ADR-019/ADR-022).

pages.title: Sub-cases
pages._note: Bespoke parent-scoped sub-case (deelzaak) list: header carries a back-to-parent button, a parent breadcrumb link and a roll-up summary line, and rows deep-link into DeelzaakDetail under the same parent route. A standard list/index type can't express the parent-route binding (/cases/:id/deelzaken) plus the parent-context header and roll-up text.

pages.title: Sub-case
pages._note: Sub-case detail that shares the `case` schema with CaseDetail but adds a mandatory always-visible parent breadcrumb (parent → current) and a link out to the canonical CaseDetail edit view. The standard detail type renders a single object with no parent-context breadcrumb or cross-route hand-off, so the parent-aware framing requires a bespoke page.

config._note: CASE archetype (AWB objection). `bezwaar` is a SUPPORTING schema linked to a unified case (bezwaar.case), and it declares NO comms linkedTypes — so NO email/calendar leaves here (those live on the parent CaseDetail). The body is the objection dossier: Overview (data+metadata), an AWB-termijnen tab grouping the statutory-clock fields (ontvangstdatum, verdaging, opschorting, ingebrekestelling/dwangsom, decisionDeadline, hearingWaived), and — because the true sub-items of a bezwaar are its committee advice requests and its decisions — related-index tabs listing bacAdviceRequest (FK bezwaar=:id) and bezwaarDecision (FK bezwaar=:id). Replaces the previously misfiled CaseTasksTab/CaseDecisionsTab, which query task.case/decision.case by the parent id and would never match a bezwaar id. Audit-trail closes the record.

DOCUMENT/decision-record archetype (beslissing op bezwaar, AWB art. 7:11). No comms linkedTypes on this schema. The body is organised as the anatomy of a formal decision: Overview (data+metadata) surfaces the disposition and the case/bezwaar link; a Motivering tab groups the reasoning fields (dispositionType, reasoning, legalBasis, advisoryOpinion, followsAdvice, deviationRationale, proceskostenvergoeding); a Rechtsmiddel tab isolates the appealNotice object (court, term, filing); a Documenten tab shows the decisionDocument/replacementDecision file references; a Bekendmaking group carries publication (publishedAt, notifiedRecipients). Audit-trail closes it. Fine-grained data groups beat a single flat form for a legally structured decision.

Deliberately MINIMAL — this is the task creation form (route /tasks/new, usually pre-seeded with ?caseId=). A blank task has no children, history or documents to show, so it is just the Overview data form plus an empty audit-trail. All richness lives on TaskDetail once the task exists.

ACTION-ITEM archetype — a work item belonging to a case (task.case), with assignee/dueDate/priority/status and an inline checklist[]. No comms linkedTypes, so no email/calendar. Overview data+metadata carries the who/when/status; a Checklist tab surfaces the checklist[] sub-items (the one array worth its own view); audit-trail records status transitions (activate/complete/terminate).

pages.title: Case map
pages._note: Full-screen split view: a filter sidebar (case type + status) beside a CnMapWidget rendering RBAC-scoped case markers with clustering and auto-fit. Markers and overview are sourced from OpenRegister's maps-overview leaf (ADR-022, OR #154). No standard page type offers the sidebar-plus-map layout or the maps-overview declaration/points fetch lifecycle.

config._note: WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (parafering/besluitvorming proposal). Kept as a bespoke full-page slot (VoorstelDetailView) rather than a widget grid: a voorstel is driven by its parafeerroute — currentStep, routeSnapshot (per-step actor/status) and the accord/return lifecycle need a live step-progress rail and inline accord/terugsturen actions that the generic data/tab grid cannot express. The view renders the proposal document + bijlagen, the linked case and decision, and the routing timeline. Metadata sidebar stays enabled for provenance.

ADVICE-REQUEST archetype (adviesAanvraag on a case). No comms linkedTypes. Overview data+metadata carries the request (case, adviseur, type, onderwerp, status) and its clock (deadline, requestedAt, receivedAt); a Vragen tab isolates the questions[] posed to the adviser; an Advies tab surfaces the returned adviesDocument file reference. Audit-trail closes it. Timeline fields sit in Overview because deadline-vs-received is the primary at-a-glance signal for an advice request.

CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (WMS/WFS map-layer definition). Admin-only, no comms. Overview data+metadata holds the endpoint config (url, layerName, srs, opacity, queryable, format, version); the standout is the preserved Verbinding-testen action tab, which live-proxies GetCapabilities against the layer so an admin can validate the endpoint from the record. No documents, no history beyond config edits — deliberately lean.

FINANCIAL-config archetype (fee by-law / legesverordening). No comms. The heart of the record is its tariff table, so the primary body tab is a related-index of the child legesartikel entries (FK verordening=:id) with create/edit/delete — the by-law IS its articles. Overview data+metadata carries the header (name, year, effectiveDate/endDate, globalMaximum, status, isActive); audit-trail records rate changes for accountability. No stat/KPI widget is used because this app's v2 renderer only ships data/metadata/related-index/audit-trail/action widgetKeys.

FINANCIAL-record archetype (fee assessment on a case). No comms — a calculation communicates through its parent case. Overview data+metadata shows the header (case, verordening, total, status, calculatedBy/calculatedAt, exportedAt). A Specificatie tab renders the inline breakdown[] line items (artikel, description, grondslag, amount, type) — the itemised bill. A Versie & correctie tab isolates the versioning trail (version, previousVersion, previousTotal, difference, correctionReason) so a reviewer can see what changed and why. Audit-trail closes it. breakdown is an embedded array (no separate legesregel entity), so it is a data-group tab, not an object-list.

CONFIG/technical archetype (multi-tenant provisioning record — legacy, superseded by OR Organisation). Admin-only, no comms. Overview data+metadata carries identity + contract (slug, displayName, legalName, kvkNumber, contractRef, tier, isolationMode, dataResidency, status). A Levenscyclus tab isolates the provisioning clock (status, createdAt, activatedAt, terminatedAt). The primary/refresh Provision + Refresh-usage admin actions are preserved; provisioning history sits in its own audit-trail tab. No documents beyond the contract reference.

CONFIG/technical archetype (initialling/approval route template). No comms. Overview data+metadata carries binding + defaults (name, caseType, voorstelType, isDefault, description). The defining content is the ordered steps[] — actor/actorType/mandatory/label per stage — so it gets its own Stappen data-group tab. Audit-trail records template edits. No documents; this is a routing definition consumed by voorstel records.

ORG-config archetype (partner organisation for cross-org case sharing). The schema is intentionally thin (name, slug, oin, contactEmail, defaultPermissionLevel, groupId, isActive) with no contact/document sub-entities, so Overview stays lean. The one relationship that matters operationally is which cases are shared with this partner, surfaced as a related-index of caseShare (FK partnerId=:id) showing the share label, type, permission and expiry. Audit-trail records activation/permission changes. No comms (contactEmail is a plain field, not a mail-leaf) and no documents.

WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (inter-organisation case handover). No comms/documents on the schema. Overview data+metadata shows the transfer request (caseId, sourceOrganization, targetOrganization, reason, requestedDate, status). A Uitkomst tab isolates the resolution fields (status, rejectionReason, completedAt) so the accept/reject outcome reads separately from the request. Audit-trail records the pending→accepted/rejected transition. Deliberately compact — a transfer is a small state machine, not a document dossier.

CONFIG/technical archetype (workflow automation handler definition). No comms. Overview data+metadata carries identity + lifecycle (slug, type, title, description, tenantId, version, isPublished, active). A Configuratie tab isolates the handler-specific config[] JSON, which is the technically interesting payload and would clutter the header if inlined. Audit-trail records publish/activation changes. No documents; this is a rule consumed by the workflow engine.

pages.title: Public appointment
pages._note: Lib gap: anonymous/token-based public pages have no v2 typed primitive — see PublicCase _note for the same architectural reason. Collapse when nc-vue adds public-page support.

pages.title: Public status
pages._note: Citizen 'track your case' page. Resolves anonymously through OpenRegister's shares-leaf #[PublicPage] endpoint GET /apps/openregister/api/public/case-tokens/{token} (ADR-022) — RBAC-respecting, public-safe fields only. Lib gap: anonymous public pages still have no v2 typed primitive; collapse when nc-vue adds public-page support.

config._note: CONFIG/technical archetype (case-workflow template — the state machine that drives cases). No comms. Overview data+metadata holds identity + lifecycle (title, caseType, version, lifecycleStatus, isActive, parentWorkflow). The two payloads that define the workflow — steps[] (stages, roles, SLAs, checklists) and transitions[] (from/to status, guards, allowed roles, actions) — get dedicated Stappen and Overgangen data-group tabs so each reads on its own. Publish/Deprecate/Clone admin actions are preserved; audit-trail records version changes.

WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (an immutable audit entry for one case status transition). No comms/documents. Overview data+metadata shows the transition (case, fromStatus→statusType, transitionLabel, noWorkflowTemplate). Because a status change is really a decision plus its side-effects, evaluatedGuards[] and dispatchedActions[] each get their own data-group tab (Guards / Acties) — showing which conditions were checked and which automatic actions fired. Audit-trail closes it. This record is itself a history entry, so it stays lean.

CONFIG/technical archetype (Landelijke Handhavingsstrategie intervention matrix — versioned, immutable enforcement policy). Admin-only, no comms/documents. Overview data+metadata carries header + axes (name, version, active, ernstAxis, gedragAxis, actorTypeAxis, createdAt). The Cellen tab renders the cells[] grid (ernst × gedrag × actorType → interventie), the matrix's substance. The Wijzigingen tab surfaces the domain auditTrail[] field (per-version actor/note), distinct from the generic audit-trail tab which records the register-level object history. lhsRecommendation records reference this matrix by version.

WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (a per-case LHS intervention recommendation derived from an lhsMatrix). No comms/documents. Overview data+metadata shows the inputs and outcome (case, inspection, ernst, gedrag, actorType, matrixVersion, recommendedInterventie, finalIntervention, recommendedBy). Because deviating from the matrix is the accountability-critical event, a Afwijking tab isolates the override fields (override, overrideJustification, overrideBy, overrideAuthority). Audit-trail closes it.

GEO-record archetype (a case location / BAG anchor). Deliberately lean: data+metadata shows address + coordinates + BAG identifiers (label, formattedAddress, latitude, longitude, nummeraanduidingId, parcelId, accuracyRadius, source) and the parent case link. NO maps leaf here — the location schema does NOT declare a maps linkedType (only the case schema does; the interactive per-case map lives on CaseDetail's Location tab and the /map overview). Audit-trail records geocoding corrections. No comms/documents.

COMMITTEE archetype (bezwaaradviescommissie / BAC). No comms leaves on the schema. Overview data+metadata carries constitution + mandate (name, type, domain, jurisdiction, chair, secretary, quorum, termStartsOn/termEndsOn, active). Because a committee is defined by its people and its caseload, a Leden tab surfaces the members[] roster (uid, role, external), and a Adviesaanvragen tab is a related-index of bacAdviceRequest (FK commissie=:id) — the advice assignments this committee is handling. Audit-trail records composition/term changes.

ADVICE archetype (a committee advice assignment on a bezwaar). No comms leaves. Overview data+metadata shows the assignment (bezwaar, commissie, panel, status, assignedAt, deadline, conclusion). A Advies tab groups the substantive opinion (advice, recommendation, conclusion, adviceIssuedAt); a Minderheidsstandpunt tab isolates dissentingOpinions[] (committee dissent is significant and shouldn't hide in the advice body); a Documenten tab collects the evidence files (adviceDocuments, signatureEvidence, hearingReportRef). Audit-trail closes it.

CASE archetype (AWB appeal at the rechtbank). `beroep` is a SUPPORTING schema linked to a unified case (beroep.case) and declares NO comms linkedTypes, so no email/calendar here (those live on the parent CaseDetail). Overview data+metadata carries the appeal header — court references and filing clock (sourceBezwaar, contestedDecision, courtReference, responsibleChamber, competentCourt, appellantFilingDate/NotifiedDate, filingDeadline, voorzieningRequested). The judicial process is split into purpose tabs: Dossierinzage (fileInspectionRequests[] — the file-inspection sub-process), Uitspraak (judgmentOutcome/judgmentDate/judgmentDocument), and Cascade (cascadeAction/cascadeBezwaarCase — the follow-on when a judgment reopens the objection). Audit-trail closes it.

pages.title: Termijn dashboard
pages._note: AWB termijnbewaking (statutory-deadline) monitor: a zaaktype filter drives a server-computed KPI bundle (total cases in period, within-term %, breached, at-risk) rendered as colour-coded compliance cards. The figures come from a dedicated deadline-aggregation endpoint, not a register query, so the standard dashboard/object-stats type can't supply or shape this data.

pages.title: Archief dashboard
pages._note: Archief e-Depot handover console: KPI cards (ready/in-progress/failed) plus trigger and batch tables and quick actions, backed by the bespoke `archief#dashboardStats` and `archief#auditLog` endpoints. The standard dashboard type renders register-derived stats only and cannot drive the e-Depot batch/trigger operational tables or handover actions.

pages.title: Tenant onboarding
pages._note: Tenant onboarding wizard view: a per-tenant 7-step progress bar plus a go-live readiness check and an activate-tenant action, rendering TenantOnboardingService progress and validateGoLive() output. This is a stateful procedure/checklist surface driven by a service, not an object listing, so no standard page type can express the step progress and go-live gating.

pages.title: Substitution
pages._note: Self-service vervanging (substitution) page: an explanatory intro about scope/permissions, a register-substitution action opening the isolated SubstitutionFormModal, and a table of the current user's own active/past substitutions filtered to where they are the absentee (enforced server-side). The standard list type can't carry the explanatory framing or the self-scoped register/revoke flow.

pages.title: Substitutions & reassignment
pages._note: Coordinator substitution console: a filterable list of all substitutions plus register-on-behalf, revoke, inspect-capacity-stamped-actions, and bulk-reassignment actions (the latter two open dedicated modals). Coordinator role is enforced server-side. The standard list type cannot host the on-behalf-of register flow, the action-list inspection, or the bulk-reassign operation over the listed objects.

observability._note: Declarative observability via OpenRegister's AppHost engine (ADR-040). Reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index, so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names (with the engine-added procest_ prefix), types, HELP texts and label keys (incl. the caseType JSON field surfacing as the case_type label) match the pre-adoption contract; the implicit procest_info / procest_up gauges are emitted by the engine. The APCu controller-local cache is replaced by the engine's per-metric cacheTtl via the distributed cache (same 30s/60s TTLs, shared across workers).
